summary: Pointe-Carleton Light: a 1919 octagonal concrete tower on Anticosti's north coast, automated in 1970. Its keepers' houses were replaced in the 1950s.

structures.note: 12 m (40 ft) base to vane per LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory; 15.9 m (52 ft) per the Québec record.

access.note: Reached by road from Port-Menier on Anticosti. Grounds open, tower closed.

events.note: Double keepers' dwelling and fog-alarm building built.
Octagonal reinforced-concrete tower completed; the Québec record dates the sector 1917 to 1919, date uncertain.
Oil tank installed at the station; listed in the Marine report printed in 1923.
Original keeper's duplex replaced by two separate residences; new fog-alarm building built.
Declared a Recognized Federal Heritage Building, per LighthouseFriends.
Sépaq abandoned the keepers' dwellings after moving its north-shore lodge.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Québec record gives 1917 to 1919 with the date marked uncertain. The 1918 Marine report says the works would be completed the next year; LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory give 1919. The story uses 1919.
LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory give 12 m (40 ft) from base to vane; the Québec record and the Amis des phares give 15.9 m (52 ft). The story gives both figures.
LighthouseFriends dates the replacement of the keeper's duplex to 1956; the Québec record says the 1950s. The French Parks Canada record (not read in full) reportedly gives 1955.

LighthouseFriends and the Lighthouse Directory say the keepers' houses have been abandoned since 2006 and are to be demolished; the Québec record says the accessory buildings have been adapted for fishers and tourists. The story reports both.

LighthouseFriends says the station is under the care of Sépaq (which rented the dwellings); the Lighthouse Directory names the Canadian Coast Guard as owner and site manager. The story names the Coast Guard as owner.

The Québec record gives 1917 to 1919 with the date marked uncertain. LighthouseFriends says the three north-shore lights were established in 1919, and the Department's report for the fiscal year ending 31 March 1918 says the plant 'will be completed next year'. The story gives the 1919 date as LighthouseFriends' and the record's range.

notes_for_editor: Verified 2026-10-27 against the Québec heritage record (id 166992, read in full), LighthouseFriends (ID 1616), the Rowlett directory (qcn.htm), the Coast Guard List of Lights (entry 1514.2), the Historic Places register text (record 10893), and the Marine report volumes (1919 volume for fiscal 1918, 1922 volume, 1923 and 1924 volumes) read through the corpus. Corrections made: the focal plane is 38.4 m (126 ft), not 38.5 m (Rowlett gives 38.5 m; the Coast Guard list gives 38.4 m); the 1919 date is described as LighthouseFriends' 'established' date and the Québec record's 1917-1919 range, instead of 'completed'; the 1918 report is now footnoted to the fiscal year ending 31 March 1918 (volume published 1919); the Sépaq wording now follows LighthouseFriends ('rented out'); the 'navigation season' phrase now follows the Coast Guard's 'seasonal' entry; the 15.9 m figure now cites the Québec record. Open items: (1) the 1920 report that LighthouseFriends quotes is the volume published 1922 in the corpus (scan p. 92, printed p. 85); the story uses that printed page. (2) Keeper dates are LighthouseFriends' only; the corpus Marine reports read did not name these keepers. (3) Keeper's house replacement: 1956 (LighthouseFriends) vs 1950s (Québec record), both stated. (4) Current use of the keepers' houses (abandoned and to be demolished, or adapted for fishers and tourists) is unresolved; the story states both. (5) Living people: Eugène Francis, Armand Lafrance, Edmour Carré and Bertrand Carré (service ending 1962-1970) are named only as LighthouseFriends lists them; no personal detail is used beyond the page's own keeper list. (6) The Parks Canada French designation page was not used. (7) No wreck or rescue is tied to this light in the sources read.
